findings.claim: Three Hay Loop tests each copy the same centreline-analysis code: the wrapped `pt(i)`, segment `heading(i)` and lap length. Two of them also copy the CORNER_RADIUS/SPAN corner-run detector almost line for line. B11 (Pine Ridge, next in the backlog) will need the same analysis and can't import any of it, so it will make a fourth copy.
findings.evidence: tests/content/hay-loop-tight.test.ts:23-57 `function corners()` and tests/content/hay-loop-corners.test.ts:17-53 `lap()` + `corners()` both declare `const CORNER_RADIUS = 80; const SPAN = 5;` and contain the same lines: `const pt = (i: number): [number, number] => c[((i % n) + n) % n] as [number, number];`, `heading(i) = headingOf(bx - ax, bz - az)`, the `length += Math.hypot(...)` loop, `const curve = (i) => wrapAngle(heading(i + SPAN) - heading(i - SPAN)) / (2 * SPAN * step);`, `const way = ...`, `while (way(start) !== 0 && start < n) start++;` and the run loop. The only difference is that tight also tracks minRadius. tests/content/hay-loop.test.ts:12-21 `geometry()` repeats the pt/heading pair a third time.
findings.suggestedFix: Owner: add a shared tests/content/centreline.ts with `centreline(trackId)` (returning n, pt, heading, step and length) and `cornerRuns(trackId, { radius, span })` (returning turn and minRadius per run). Import them in the three Hay Loop tests. A night can create that new file now so B11 imports it instead of copying, but changing the three existing files needs the owner.

findings.claim: hay-loop-bales.test.ts writes its own oriented-box corner function and SAT overlap test. tests/sim/helpers.ts already exports both as boxCorners and polygonOverlap, which the other prop-overlap tests use.
findings.evidence: tests/content/hay-loop-bales.test.ts:9-23 `function corners(b: Box)` builds the 4 corners from fx=sin h, fz=-cos h and HAY_BALE_LENGTH/2, HAY_BALE_WIDTH/2. :25-36 `function overlap(a, b)` is a hand-rolled separating-axis check. tests/sim/helpers.ts:291 `export function boxCorners(x, z, heading, halfLength, halfWidth)` (doc: 'Corners of an oriented box (hay bale)') and :261 `export function polygonOverlap(a, b)` ('Overlap depth of two convex polygons by the separating axis theorem').
findings.suggestedFix: Owner: replace corners/overlap with `polygonOverlap(boxCorners(a.x, a.z, a.heading, HAY_BALE_LENGTH / 2, HAY_BALE_WIDTH / 2), boxCorners(b.x, …)) > 1e-6` imported from ../sim/helpers.ts.

findings.claim: The three B07 best-lap tests copy their helpers. The m:ss.cc formatter `fmt` appears three times, `visibleNewBest` twice, and new-best-chip's `twinRace` repeats the loop of the shared twinPlayerInputs. All three also keep the stale `playerLivery` render mock. None of these files is among C019's six.
findings.evidence: fmt, identical body `const cs = Math.round(t / 10); return `${Math.floor(cs / 6000)}:${String(Math.floor((cs % 6000) / 100)).padStart(2, '0')}.${…}``, at tests/ui/new-best-chip.test.ts:42-45, tests/game/best-lap-persistence.test.ts:37-40 and tests/game/best-lap-storage-blocked.test.ts:29-32. tests/ui/results-screen.test.ts:4 already imports formatTime from src/ui/format.ts:14 instead. visibleNewBest is identical at new-best-chip.test.ts:85-93 and best-lap-persistence.test.ts:57-65. new-best-chip.test.ts:27-38 `twinRace()` repeats tests/game/helpers.ts:9-20 twinPlayerInputs line for line, adding only `lapTicks`. Stale mock `playerLivery: (n) => …` at new-best-chip.test.ts:14, best-lap-persistence.test.ts:13, best-lap-storage-blocked.test.ts:11 and gamepad-menu.test.ts:13.
findings.suggestedFix: Owner: export `lapTime(ms)` (or reuse formatTime) and `visibleNewBest(root)` from tests/game/helpers.ts. Replace twinRace's loop with twinPlayerInputs(TRACK, SEED, 2, 36000) and read the lap ticks from a replayed world or the game. Drop the playerLivery mock lines in these files, together with C019's.

findings.claim: Three keycap-legend tests each write their own matchMedia stub. Two of them are the same media-query evaluator, one with the device fixed and one taking it as a parameter. No shared stub exists in tests/ui/helpers.ts, so the next desktop or reduced-motion UI test (B08/B09 are in flight) will copy it a fourth time.
findings.evidence: tests/ui/keycap-legend.test.ts:19-35 `function useDevice(d: Device)` and tests/ui/keycap-legend-keys.test.ts:11-27 `function useDesktop()` share the same body: `query.split(/\s+and\s+/).every((part) => { const m = /\(\s*([\w-]+)\s*:\s*([\w.]+?)(px)?\s*\)/.exec(part); … })`, then `vi.stubGlobal('matchMedia', (query) => { const list = new EventTarget() as MediaQueryList; Object.assign(list, { media: query, matches: …, onchange: null, addListener() {}, removeListener() {} }); return list; })`. keycap-legend-keys only fixes d = 1440×900 fine. tests/ui/keycap-legend-slide-state.test.ts:11-17 is a third stub with `matches: !query.includes('coarse')`.
findings.suggestedFix: Owner: move `useDevice(d)` and a `DESKTOP` constant into a shared test helper and call `useDevice(DESKTOP)` from all three files. A night may create the helper as a new file (e.g. tests/ui/media.ts) so new tests import it, but changing the three existing files needs the owner.
